why: Asia is a Roman province, not a single place, and Bible Atlas's point lies inland of its coast; the seven churches are drawn individually.
Here Israel means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
3:12 speaks of the new Jerusalem coming down out of heaven, not the earthly city where Bible Atlas puts its point.
The chapter describes God's throne and does not name or title Jesus; the Lamb first appears in chapter 5.
Here Israel, Gad, Reuben, Asher, Manasseh, Issachar, Levi, Simeon, Benjamin, Joseph and Zebulun mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
The "breath of life from God" (11:11) is not named as the Holy Spirit. In 11:8 Sodom and Egypt are symbolic names for the great city, so a dot on the Dead Sea or in Egypt would mislead.
Neither Jesus nor a title for him is named in this chapter. Many readers hear his voice in "I am coming like a thief" (16:15), but that is an inference.

Revelation 20:8 uses Gog and Magog as names for the nations "at the four corners of the earth" and gives no location. The point north of the Caucasus follows one reading of Ezekiel 38-39. The place entries stay linked; the ancestor Magog and the prince Gog are not meant.

The holy city here is the new Jerusalem coming down out of heaven (21:2, 21:10), not the earthly city where Bible Atlas puts its point. Here Israel means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
